newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares open steady, wait for U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: German shares open steady, wait for U.S. data.

text.p: German shares opened steady on Friday in thin trade following Thursday's national holiday and were cautious ahead of U.S. jobs data due out at 1230 GMT, traders said.

The DAX index of 30 blue chip shares opened floor trade at 2,676.09 points, down 0.41 from Wednesday's close. By mid-session the index was up 3.10 at 2679.60, just below its record high of 2680.10 reached during Wednesday's session.
Dealers said the share market was supported by the dollar's strength against the mark which aids export-oriented German shares.
Following the Germany Unity Day holiday on Thursday many people had taken a long weekend. "It's a kind of half holiday so turnover should be pretty thin," said one trader.
Volume was also limited ahead of the release of U.S. jobless figures. "Traders aren't going to want to stick their neck out ahead of the unemployment figures," said one dealer.
Traders said players on the sidelines could come back into the market later in the day and the DAX index could then test the psychological and technical level of 2,700 points.

Building group Holzmann AG was the loss leader, tumbling 22 marks to 328 marks, after a Bild newspaper report said that its chief executive could be sacked and replaced by the head of diversified industrial group Metallgesellschaft AG.
MG denied the report as nonsense. A Holzmann spokesman was unable to comment immediately. Holzmann on Wednesday denied reports that the group had liquidity problems.
Meanwhile chemical stocks were ahead of the market with both Bayer and BASF firmer, mirroring strength in U.S. chemicals overnight, dealers said.
